📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Zonveer ZX3 is one of the best values I’ve seen in electric off-road riding, and one of the most fun things I’ve ridden to date – value for the dollar. Its Black Friday sale brings the 2,800W electric dirt bike down to $1,299, $500 off its $1,799 list price.

It has been revealed that for that money, you get a 1,200Wh battery, dual hydraulic disc brakes, and full suspension in a 130 lb package. That’s a great entry point for beginners.

Zonveer is a young brand. It rolled out in the US in March with two bikes, the kid-sized DX1 and the ZX3, and it’s run by United Mobility, which lists its address in Dover, Delaware. It sells direct and ships from US warehouses, and Zonveer also sells the ZX3 across Europe under its own brand through its EU store.

Here’s what the ZX3 brings, according to Zonveer’s product page:.

A hub motor means there’s no motor chain to maintain, and the NFC card and PIN unlock mean there’s no app to fight with. I like that.

It has been revealed that zonveer sent me a ZX3 to test, and I’m impressed with what they shipped, knowing the cost. It isn’t trying to be a race bike. And it doesn’t need to be. Here’s my first ride review:.

According to recent reports, with 2,800W peak, it’s somewhat modest by e-moto standards. That’s exactly what makes it approachable for someone who has never ridden a dirt bike: the power is enough to have a blast on trails without being intimidating.

My girlfriend had never ridden a dirt bike before, and she got comfortable within a few minutes, and she was hooked as soon as she got the hang of it.

And while testing with my girlfriend, it was clear this bike makes the most sense for lighter riders. Zonveer claims it climbs slopes of up to 30 degrees, which is optimistic for anyone over ~175 lbs, like myself. It still climbed some of the worst slopes on my land, but it did so with some difficulty, which wasn’t the case for some of my lighter friends who also rode it.

It has been revealed that range is the other claim to take with a grain of salt. Riding 45 miles on 1,200Wh means using under 27Wh per mile, which is e-bike efficiency on a 130 lb dirt bike with knobby tires. It’s still a lot of energy, and you can ride this long distances at lower speeds. Just expect less if you ride it hard, and that’s where the fun is at.

Zonveer’s Black Friday sale has the ZX3 at $1,299, and the company gave Electrek readers the code ELECTREK for an extra 5% off, which brings it down to $1,234.05.

Recent findings suggest that the sale also includes a free water bottle and lock, and can be combined for a two-pack of ZX3s for $2,599. Shipping is free, the warranty is one year, Zonveer told us it accepts returns within 30 days on bikes ridden less than 10 miles, with a $200 restocking fee. Here’s the full refund policy.

Recent findings suggest that we’ve ridden a lot of electric two-wheelers, and the ZX3 is one of the most fun per dollar. At $1,299, or about $1,234 with our code, it’s hard to find another 1,200Wh electric dirt bike with dual hydraulic disc brakes and full suspension from a brand that ships from US warehouses.

It has been revealed that it’s not fast by e-moto standards, and the range and climbing claims are optimistic. But for beginners, and especially lighter riders, the power lands right in that sweet spot of manageable fun. It’s a bike you can learn on without scaring yourself, and it’s cheap enough that a family can buy two for less than one Sur-Ron.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • US prosecutors are seeking more than $1.1 billion in USDC stolen during the October Binance hack without accessing the attackers' wallets.
  • It has been revealed that the Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint in Washington, D.C., on Nov.
  • Under the proposed recovery arrangement, stablecoin issuer Circle would create an equivalent amount of latest USDC and transfer it to the US government if the court approves the forfeiture.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

US prosecutors are seeking more than $1.1 billion in USDC stolen during the October Binance hack without accessing the attackers' wallets.

It has been revealed that the Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 23, targeting frozen USDC associated with 36 wallet and smart-contract addresses across 18 blockchains.

Under the proposed recovery arrangement, stablecoin issuer Circle would create an equivalent amount of latest USDC and transfer it to the US government if the court approves the forfeiture.

The original tokens would remain frozen in addresses allegedly controlled by the hackers.

Sources indicate that circle had already blocked approximately $1.1 billion in USDC following the Oct. 29 attack, which US authorities attributed to North Korea's Lazarus Group.

However, the firm cannot directly transfer the frozen tokens because it does not control the private keys associated with the attackers' wallets.

Instead, its ability to block transfers and matter replacement tokens provides prosecutors with a mechanism to recover the value of stolen assets without obtaining the underlying wallets.

The forfeiture complaint describes a substitute payment to the U.S. government.

The proposed transfer would use new USDC equal to the blocked amount.

The complaint leaves the eventual treatment of the original tokens unspecified.

Recent findings suggest that the two tracks distinguish Circle’s existing transfer restriction from the conditional substitute issuance described in paragraph 34 of the federal complaint. No figures are calculated.

The complaint leaves the eventual treatment of the original tokens unspecified.

Meanwhile, prosecutors are seeking a further restraining order to keep the stolen USDC immobilized while the forfeiture case proceeds.

The proposed arrangement highlights the recovery powers available through centrally issued stablecoins, unlike native Bitcoin and Ethereum, which a token issuer cannot freeze.

The Justice Department said US authorities have helped freeze, seize, or return more than $2.9 billion in cryptocurrencies since the attack, which resulted in over $6 billion in losses.

Binance welcomed the recovery effort, confirming that it was working with U.S. authorities and industry partners to retrieve stolen assets.

“We are coordinating closely with the US Department of Justice, as well as with industry partners who have assisted in freezing assets impacted by the incident.”.

Binance added that it would continue cooperating throughout the forfeiture proceedings to support the return of affected funds.

Industry observers note that the exchange previously said it had replaced all affected customer token assets with its own funds by Nov. 13, drawing on its corporate treasury, futures insurance fund and emergency reserves.

Meanwhile, Binance announced the appointment of Mandiant, SlowMist and Verichains to conduct independent reviews of its security procedures following the attack.

The firms will examine its existing security infrastructure, identify potential weaknesses and assess its defenses against future cyberattacks.

Mandiant specializes in incident response and nation-state cyber threats, while SlowMist and Verichains provide blockchain security research and threat intelligence.

Binance Chief Security Officer Jimmy Su said the tech giant was committed to acting on the reviewers' findings.

The announcement follows court filings describing how attackers allegedly compromised a Binance employee through malicious software distributed during a fraudulent recruitment interview before gaining control of exchange wallets.

The security reviews have not yet produced findings, leaving Binance's next defensive changes dependent on their conclusions.

While this marks an historic milestone in the Bitcoin bear market, Grayscale further disclosed an interesting twist that makes the current bear market pretty different from previous times.

The source confirmed that this bear market has been relatively mild in terms of price losses despite lasting longer than previous downturns.

All through the current bear market, Bitcoin has only posted a price decrease 56%, suggesting that it has suffered considerably smaller losses than several previous bear markets.

This means that even though Bitcoin has spent more than a year in a bear market, its decline has not been as severe as those seen in earlier cycles.

To back the data, Grayscale showed charts comparing Bitcoin's performance across historical bear markets that ended in June 2011, December 2013, December 2017, November 2021, and the ongoing October 2025 cycle.

While the 2011, 2017 and 2021 bear cycles suffered massive losses, especially during the former when its indexed performance fell below 10, the current 2025 bear market broke historical pattern by enduring a longer period yet a comparatively modest decline in Bitcoin’s price.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that the trim lasted just over nine months.
  • Here’s what Tesla’s US Model Y design studio lists as of today (prices before the destination fee):.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that tesla has pulled the $41,990 Model Y All-Wheel Drive from its US online configurator. The cheapest dual-motor Model Y you can order now is the Model Y Premium AWD at $49,990, an $8,000 jump.

Industry observers note that the trim lasted just over nine months. Tesla debuted it in early February, and it’s gone without a word from the tech giant.

Here’s what Tesla’s US Model Y design studio lists as of today (prices before the destination fee):.

When Tesla introduced the base Model Y AWD in February, it was basically the stripped-down Model Y with a second motor. It had 294 miles of range, did 0-60 mph in 4.6 seconds and kept the same cut-down cabin as the base RWD. At a $2,000 premium over the single-motor version, it was the most sensible AWD pricing Tesla had offered in years.

Sources indicate that and the AWD trim isn’t the only change. In February, the Premium RWD cost $44,990 and the Premium AWD cost $48,990. Both are now $1,000 higher.

Add it up and the cheapest all-wheel-drive Model Y went from $41,990 to $49,990 in nine months. That’s a 19% increase.

In a recent development, the timing isn’t great for Tesla’s competitive position. Chevrolet’s 2027 Equinox EV LT 1 AWD starts at $40,295 before destination, with 307 miles of EPA range. Ford’s Mustang Mach-E Select AWD starts at $40,795.

Both now undercut Tesla’s cheapest AWD crossover by more than $9,000.

Recent findings suggest that if you live somewhere it snows and you were shopping for a upcoming Model Y, the math just got a lot worse. You can still find some base AWD units in Tesla’s inventory, but once those are gone, that’s it.

This is also the latest cut in a year of Tesla shrinking its lineup. Elon Musk killed the Model S and Model X in January to free up Fremont for Optimus, and Cybertruck production is winding down. Meanwhile, the most recent new Tesla is the $61,990 Model Y L, which sits at the top of the range, not the bottom.

We liked this trim. It was the first time in a long time that Tesla treated all-wheel drive as a $2,000 option rather than a huge upsell bundled with a nicer interior, and it put the Model Y right in the price bracket of the Equinox EV and Mach-E with AWD.

Now it’s gone, and the Premium trims went up $1,000 on top of that. Tesla didn’t explain either move. It rarely does anymore.

Sources indicate that there are two plausible reasons. Either Tesla is tight on Model Y build slots and would rather fill them with higher-margin Premium trims, or the cheap AWD simply wasn’t selling. We don’t know which. But both explanations land in the same place for buyers: a more expensive Model Y.

According to recent reports, tesla is not going to keep 6 different model Y trims especially when the most expensive trim in the Model YL is selling. They will definitely squeeze out as much money from selling more expensive trims so the lowest end trim will most likely be next to go.

According to recent reports, and Tesla has a habit of this. The “Standard” name for its cheaper Model Y and Model 3 lasted a few months. The single-motor Cybertruck, the only version that made sense, was gone within days. Cheaper trims show up, get a news cycle, and quietly disappear.

That’s a problem for a company whose consumer lineup is shrinking down to two cars. The Model Y is Tesla’s volume. Thinning it out at the bottom is the opposite of what you’d do if growing EV sales were the priority.

How long before the $39,990 RWD goes the same way?

It has been revealed that data from Yahoo Finance showed that American Bitcoin shares climbed as high as $4.38 during Monday's trading before closing 16.3% higher at $4.07. Despite the rebound, the stock remains approximately 84% below its level at the start of the year.

The financing comes as the manufacturer continues expanding its Bitcoin holdings, which recently surpassed 8,500 BTC.

American Bitcoin said the accumulation has moved it from 15th to 13th among publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holders worldwide.

The firm combines Bitcoin mining with direct accumulation, making the preservation of its reserves central to its long-term strategy.

“This $150 million facility provides American Bitcoin with non-dilutive capital to support our continued operations and growth initiatives.”.

The approach contrasts with a broader shift across the mining industry.

Recent findings suggest that blockchain analytics firm Glassnode reported that publicly listed miners in its tracked group had reduced their combined Bitcoin reserves by nearly half since January. The firm attributed the decline to miners increasingly using Bitcoin holdings to finance their expansion into artificial intelligence data centers.

Sources indicate that for years, many publicly traded miners retained their mined Bitcoin and sometimes purchased additional coins. That strategy has increasingly given way to asset sales as operators redirect capital toward AI computing infrastructure.

American Bitcoin's arrangement offers another financing route, allowing it to retain ownership of its Bitcoin while pledging some holdings as collateral for dollar liquidity.

The agreement allows American Bitcoin's subsidiary to borrow up to $150 million from FalconX Charlie, secured by Bitcoin held at Anchorage Digital Bank.

It has been revealed that according to the SEC filing, borrowings carry a 5.95% annual loan fee, alongside commitment fees on unused capacity. The facility matures in November 2028, with a possible three-year extension.

However, preserving Bitcoin through collateralized borrowing introduces exposure to forced asset sales during market downturns.

The agreement requires pledged Bitcoin to cover at least 143% of outstanding principal when funds are drawn. If that ratio falls below 130%, FalconX can demand additional Bitcoin or partial repayment to restore the collateral requirement.

American Bitcoin’s subsidiary had drawn nothing on the $150 million FalconX line as of the Nov. 23 filing. These thresholds govern draws and outstanding loans.

The 143% ratio serves as the draw minimum and the target after a margin-call top-up or partial collateral release.

The graphic highlights the agreement’s thresholds for draws and outstanding principal. It does not show a reported collateral balance or forecast a sale.

It has been revealed that markers are spaced proportionately on each axis using the contractual ratio of pledged bitcoin value to total outstanding principal. Thresholds come from Item 1.01, the master agreement and the signed term sheet.

Sources indicate that the graphic indicates the agreement’s thresholds for draws and outstanding principal. It does not show a reported collateral balance or forecast a sale.

A decline below 105% can trigger default and potentially allow the lender to liquidate pledged assets under the agreement's conditions.

At the minimum initial collateral ratio, a Bitcoin price decline of about 9.1% would trigger a margin call if the firm borrowed and neither added collateral nor repaid debt.

American Bitcoin already had 3,090 BTC pledged for mining equipment purchases as of Sept. 30, according to its quarterly filing.

The new facility could let it access more capital while maintaining its Bitcoin position, but borrowing would also put additional holdings behind collateral obligations.

Still, the arrangement leaves American Bitcoin on a different path from miners selling reserves to fund AI infrastructure, with its ability to retain those coins increasingly tied to BTC's market value and how much it ultimately borrows.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor sees new ways to put Bitcoin (BTC) to work on Wall Street.
  • According to staff at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), Bitcoin can be used to meet certain financial resource requirements for U.S.
  • ‘Next step for adoption is using Bitcoin to work,’ Saylor wrote on X in response to the CFTC advisory published on Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor sees new ways to put Bitcoin (BTC) to work on Wall Street.

According to staff at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), Bitcoin can be used to meet certain financial resource requirements for U.S. derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses.

‘Next step for adoption is using Bitcoin to work,’ Saylor wrote on X in response to the CFTC advisory published on Nov. 23.

As per the guidance, these companies must maintain sufficient financial resources to cover their operating costs for at least a year.

Industry observers note that as clarified by CFTC staff, Bitcoin and Ether can be used to meet this requirement (as well as payment stablecoins). The advisory also provides guidance on how staff interpret the current rules. It also applies to swap execution facilities (SEFs), which are platforms where counterparties trade swaps.

Bitcoin holdings worth $10 million could count for $8 million toward the annual requirement, based on the minimum 20% discount that CFTC staff noted they would accept. This provides some flexibility in case Bitcoin's price falls. The discount is also called a haircut.

Recent findings suggest that for Ether, the same minimum 20% haircut applies. For payment stablecoins, the haircut is 2%.

This provides some incentive for an exchange to actually hold BTC. Exchanges could hold Bitcoin on their balance sheets and use some of its value to satisfy this reserve requirement. There would be no need to sell it for USD first.

However, a futures exchange still needs to have sufficient unencumbered cash or highly liquid securities to cover its operating costs for at least six months. Bitcoin, Ether and even payment stablecoins do not fall into this category.

In a recent development, the same six-month liquidity requirement applies to clearinghouses. Additionally, they need to maintain sufficient financial resources to cover a default by a clearing member.

CFTC staff also noted a potential downside for exchanges holding crypto reserves. During a market slump, there's a risk that an exchange's operating losses might rise. At the same time, the value of the Bitcoin it holds to cover those losses might fall.

So this possibility should be considered before an exchange decides whether to use Bitcoin to meet its financial resource requirements.

Latest Update: Strategy sells $176M in MSTR shares for STRC buybacks – What’s behind the shift?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (458 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Michael Saylor’s Strategy is making headlines, but there is something under the wraps that is raising eyebrows.
  • In its 23rd November Form 8-K filing, the Bitcoin [BTC] DAT revealed that the tech giant is becoming more aggressive with its capital management strategy, particularly when it comes to its preferred stock, STRC.
  • In fact, between 16th and 22nd November, the firm sold 1,925,676 shares of its Class A common stock (MSTR), generating $176.7 million in net proceeds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Michael Saylor’s Strategy is making headlines, but there is something under the wraps that is raising eyebrows.

In its 23rd November Form 8-K filing, the Bitcoin [BTC] DAT revealed that the tech giant is becoming more aggressive with its capital management strategy, particularly when it comes to its preferred stock, STRC.

In fact, between 16th and 22nd November, the firm sold 1,925,676 shares of its Class A common stock (MSTR), generating $176.7 million in net proceeds.

But here’s a catch: instead of directing the entire amount towards Bitcoin purchases, Strategy used just $29.6 million to acquire 457 BTC while allocating the remaining proceeds towards repurchasing STRC shares.

It has been revealed that at the same time, the organization bought back 2,183,747 STRC shares for approximately $211.8 million during the same period, using $147 million from MSTR share sales and another $64.8 million from its USD cash balance. Naturally, this has raised an important question: why is Strategy selling one security to buy back another?

Recent findings suggest that so, the difference lies in the roles of MSTR and STRC. MSTR, as we all know now, is Strategy’s common stock, offering investors exposure to its Bitcoin holdings and business performance. STRC, meanwhile, is a variable-rate perpetual preferred stock with a $100 stated value that pays regular dividends.

According to recent reports, therefore, Strategy aims to keep STRC trading around 99-100. When it trades below this range, buybacks can help support its market price while reducing outstanding shares and future dividend obligations.

It has been revealed that this also explains the tech giant’s expanded buyback capacity. On 23rd November, Strategy increased its Digital Credit Securities repurchase authorization from $3 billion to $4 billion, with approximately $1.12 billion remaining. At the same time, it continues to use its ATM program to raise capital by issuing MSTR shares.

Given such a change in intends, Strategy still continues to be the largest BTC holder, with a total of 851,305 BTC, acquired at an aggregate cost of $64.23 billion and an average purchase price of $75,446 per BTC.

All in all, the filing shows that Strategy is balancing Bitcoin accumulation with preferred stock buybacks rather than directing all its capital towards BTC purchases.

This comes as the MSTR stock was trading at $84.40 at press time up by 8.48% in the past 24 hours. Meanwhile, STRC was trading at $98.26 at press time up by 5.01% in the past trading day.

Lastly, AMBCrypto’s recent report also highlighted this shift, as its MSTR shares were facing mounting pressure from Bitcoin’s decline, losing over 40% in Q4 2026.

However, one thing is clear, and that is continued MSTR weakness could make fresh capital raises more difficult, threatening Strategy’s future Bitcoin accumulation looks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Electric truck operator Nevoya is expanding its deal with Meta with the fresh deployment of 25 Class 8 battery-electric trucks on the Interstate 10 (I-10) between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona … but Meta won’t be shipping any products.

According to recent reports, the second major trucking deal between Facebook parent organization Meta and electric truck operator Nevoya will put 25 latest battery-electric semis on I-10, running freight between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona. But Meta isn’t buying trucks, hiring drivers or shipping its own products. Instead, Zuck’s company helping pay for someone else’s cleaner freight through environmental attribute certificates (EACs), a carbon credit mechanism that lets companies claim the emissions benefits of electric trucking without operating the trucks themselves.

According to recent reports, “Coming back to Nevoya for a second corridor reflects what we look for in our value chain work: partners that can scale, and agreements we can repeat, mentioned Devon Lake, Head of Net Zero Strategy, Meta. “Freight is part of the emissions footprint of building and operating our data centers, and multi-year commitments like this help address our scope 3 emissions and make electric trucking available and competitive on the routes that serve the regions where we build.”.

Industry observers note that meta was one of several buyers in the DC-based Center for Green Market Activation (GMA) buyers’ alliance. The group’s collective EAC purchases supported Nevoya’s initial 63-truck deployment on the Houston–Dallas corridor back in May. This new Agreement, however, is a standalone deal between Nevoya and Meta only, and gives Meta an established framework to open more electric truck corridors in the future.

This clever application of these agreements is what makes the Dallas-Houston run stand out, with GMA calling it, “the first large-scale application of book and claim to zero-emission trucking.” The company adds that this arrangement helps client companies overcome existing barriers to EV adoption while enabling Nevoya to deploy new trucks, “where they deliver the strongest commercial and operational value.”.

Each account trading on the XRP Ledger's decentralized exchange moved an average of 4,328 XRP a day in the third quarter of 2026, up 437% from 805 XRP in the same quarter a year earlier, according to a report that XRP treasury organization Evernorth released on Tuesday.

According to recent reports, according to Evernorth, the average swap on the XRP Ledger reached 35 XRP in the third quarter, up from 19 XRP in the second quarter and under 6 XRP a year earlier. "The growth came from bigger trades, not more of them," the tech giant wrote in the report.

Industry observers note that at the same time, the number of accounts trading on the XRP Ledger's order book fell to 1,042 a day in the third quarter of 2026 from 2,027 a day in the third quarter of 2025. The number stood at 1,203 in the fourth quarter of 2025, 1,324 in the first quarter of 2026 and 1,125 in the second quarter, according to the report.

Order-book volume on the XRP Ledger rose to 4.51 million XRP a day in the third quarter from 1.63 million XRP a day a year earlier, Evernorth data shows.

In total, 5.16 million XRP a day was traded on the XRP Ledger's exchange in the third quarter, and the figure was up 96% year over year, according to Evernorth.

Industry observers note that measured in U.S. dollars, exchange volume on the XRP Ledger fell 15% year over year in the third quarter of 2026, according to the report.

Evernorth also compared the XRP Ledger with Ethereum, BNB Chain, Solana, Base, Arbitrum, Avalanche and Polygon. Across these seven networks, exchange volume in dollars fell 42% over the same period, the report shows.

XRP was trading at around $0.93 on Tuesday morning after reaching as high as $1.026 on Monday, according to CoinMarketCap.

Sources indicate that the report also highlights that the average balance of Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin on the XRP Ledger reached $937 million in the third quarter of 2026, up from $539 million in the second quarter. By the end of the quarter, the RLUSD balance on the XRP Ledger stood at $1.15 billion, compared with $670 million at the end of the second quarter, and the number of RLUSD holders on the network rose to 67,449 from 45,620.

According to Evernorth, the XRP Ledger's average share of RLUSD reached 48.5% in the third quarter, up from 34% in the second quarter. Still, Ethereum finished the quarter with more RLUSD than the XRP Ledger. Evernorth noted that on Ethereum, RLUSD "can already be lent," and that on the XRP Ledger, "native lending is in validator voting.".

As of Nov. 20, the Lending Protocol amendment had 24 of 35 validator votes, according to XRPScan. The amendment needs 29 votes, held for 14 days, to activate.

Evernorth completed its business combination with Armada Acquisition Corp. II on Oct. 9, and its shares began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker XRPN on Oct. 12. The manufacturer entered the public markets holding approximately 473 million XRP, according to its press release.

Evernorth revealed the deal in October 2025, with investments from SBI, Ripple, Pantera Capital, Kraken and GSR.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hong Kong plans to require banks to register with its securities regulator before offering crypto custody services to customers.
  • The government published the Virtual Asset Services Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2026 on Nov.
  • Industry observers note that under the legislation, banks and stored-value facility operators already supervised by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) would need additional registration with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) to provide covered virtual asset services.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hong Kong plans to require banks to register with its securities regulator before offering crypto custody services to customers.

The government published the Virtual Asset Services Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2026 on Nov. 20, expanding its regulatory framework to cover businesses safeguarding, trading, advising on or managing virtual assets.

Industry observers note that under the legislation, banks and stored-value facility operators already supervised by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) would need additional registration with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) to provide covered virtual asset services. Independent providers would generally need an SFC license.

Hong Kong’s bill would generally require a license for standalone custodians and registration for HKMA-supervised banks and stored value facility licensees.

Both forms of authorization would come from the Securities and Futures Commission.

According to recent reports, the diagram covers the proposed authorization routes. Exceptions and implementation timing depend on the legislation.

The two routes follow the government’s gazettal announcement and the earlier custody consultation. Existing bank standards follow the HKMA’s May 2026 guidance.

Recent findings suggest that the diagram covers the proposed authorization routes. Exceptions and implementation timing depend on the legislation.

The bill, scheduled for its first reading in the Legislative Council on Dec. 2, would amend Hong Kong's Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance. Applicants would face fit-and-proper assessments and other regulatory requirements designed to strengthen investor protection.

The additional requirements build on existing regulatory obligations for banks entering the digital asset market.

In May, the HKMA updated its guidance requiring financial institutions offering digital asset custody to maintain appropriate security, governance and operational controls.

Banks intending to launch such services must consult the monetary authority beforehand and demonstrate compliance with its custody standards.

The regulatory expansion comes amid growing institutional interest in digital assets, although security concerns and regulatory uncertainty have slowed adoption.

Industry observers note that A February report by Ripple and Quinlan & Associates found that 77% of 65 surveyed Hong Kong financial institutions had either adopted digital assets or planned to do so. However, only 25% had adopted them at the time of the survey.

The research found that 65% of respondents preferred outsourcing custody, rising to 80% among buy-side institutions.

Bank-affiliated custodians attracted the strongest institutional interest, with 64% of respondents expressing willingness to engage them. However, only 40% rated their readiness highly.

Hong Kong's proposed custody framework targets the security risks associated with controlling customers' digital assets.

In their December 2025 consultation conclusions, the SFC and the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau identified the safeguarding of private keys and similar instruments that enable asset transfers as the central activity requiring authorization.

Regulators stated businesses controlling these instruments face technological and operational risks that could result in the loss or unauthorized transfer of customers' assets.

Fund managers and other institutions that delegate custody to third parties without safeguarding private keys would generally fall outside the specific custody licensing requirement.

In a recent development, similarly, noncustodial wallet providers that let customers retain independent control of their assets would generally not require authorization. Shared-key arrangements would be assessed based on the provider's ability to transfer assets and customers' ability to retain or recover access independently.

The proposed virtual asset custody regime would exclude tokenized securities, which remain subject to existing securities regulations.

Existing crypto custodians could face more immediate compliance pressures once the legislation takes effect.

During the consultation process, some industry participants requested transitional arrangements lasting between three and 18 months, citing potential operational disruptions and the time needed to meet regulatory requirements.

However, authorities rejected automatically granting existing operators temporary authorization, citing concerns about investor protection and confusion over their regulatory status.

Instead, regulators proposed expedited approvals for certain banks, bank subsidiaries and entities associated with licensed crypto trading platforms that had already undergone supervisory assessments.

Authorities also encouraged existing custodians to begin engaging with the SFC or HKMA ahead of the new regime.

While the bill is scheduled to reach the Legislative Council on Dec. 2, the government has yet to announce a commencement date. That decision will determine how much time existing custodians have to secure authorization and avoid disruptions to their businesses.

Breaking: Here are the coolest e-motorcycles and gear we saw at EICMA 2026

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every year, the world’s largest motorcycle companies (and plenty of the world’s smallest motorcycle companies, too) converge on Milan, Italy for Europe’s premier motorcycle showcase.
  • Below is a list of the best things I saw while walking around the show this year, presented in no particular order.
  • LiveWire came to EICMA with perhaps its most diverse electric two-wheeler lineup yet, showing just how far the firm has expanded beyond the premium electric motorcycles that originally defined the Harley-Davidson spin-off.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every year, the world’s largest motorcycle companies (and plenty of the world’s smallest motorcycle companies, too) converge on Milan, Italy for Europe’s premier motorcycle showcase. That means that all of the newest electric motorcycle announcements happen in one place, and we get a chance to check out the coolest developments and most interesting newly introduced gear.

Below is a list of the best things I saw while walking around the show this year, presented in no particular order.

LiveWire came to EICMA with perhaps its most diverse electric two-wheeler lineup yet, showing just how far the firm has expanded beyond the premium electric motorcycles that originally defined the Harley-Davidson spin-off.

Sources indicate that the latest S4 Honcho family was a major focus, including the street-oriented Honcho Street, off-road Honcho Trail, and newly unveiled Honcho Skate, a stripped-down addition to the modular platform. The booth also included LiveWire’s larger S2 electric motorcycles, creating a pretty broad spectrum from lightweight urban machines up through full-size highway-capable electric motorcycles.

The other major piece of the booth was DUST Moto, which LiveWire acquired earlier this year. The production-intent DUST Hightail was displayed alongside the newly revealed DUST Spur, giving LiveWire an immediate presence in the increasingly popular lightweight electric dirt bike category.

Add in STACYC’s electric balance bikes for young riders, and the entire booth almost looked like an electric two-wheeler progression chart: start a kid on a STACYC, move up through lightweight DUST and Honcho machines, and eventually graduate to a full-size LiveWire.

GR1T Motorcycles is a relatively young European electric motorcycle startup that caught my eye at EICMA with its G1 platform, a lightweight electric motorcycle designed and engineered in Italy. The basic recipe is pretty compelling: 130 km/h (81 mph) top speed, 11 kW of continuous power and 26.6 kW (36 hp) peak, all while weighing just 130 kg (287 lb).

Perhaps most importantly for urban riders, its roughly 6 kWh battery is actually split into two removable 3 kWh packs, meaning apartment dwellers can pull the batteries out and charge them inside. They’re massive, but removing them is doable.

GR1T’s bikes therefore pack in around 50% more battery capacity than most electric motorcycles in this size and weight class, meaning roughly 50% more range, as well.

There are also some interesting and clever design choices, like the underslung rear suspension and the triple-camera system that includes front and rear dashcams plus a cockpit-facing camera for recording the rider.

The clever part of the overall design scheme is that GR1T isn’t developing a separate platform for every motorcycle. The same basic G1 chassis, motor, batteries, belt drive, and electronics underpin four versions: the G1S Street, G1X Scrambler, G1XR Raider, and utility-oriented G1M Mission.

Prices are set to start at €8,495 including VAT, putting these squarely in that emerging category of reasonably affordable, lightweight electric motorcycles that have enough speed for real-world commuting without chasing superbike performance.

There’s an important caveat, though: these aren’t production motorcycles yet. GR1T says it is right now fundraising, with factory development and pre-orders set to follow after funding closes and first deliveries now targeted for the first half of 2028.

So the bikes aren’t quite ready for primetime yet, but it’s definitely a organization to watch.

Real Motors brought one of the more visually striking electric motorcycles to EICMA with Project: ARES, a futuristic electric café racer that the American startup describes as an “Electric Analog” machine – basically an attempt to preserve the raw, mechanical connection of motorcycling while ditching unnecessary screens and gadgetry.

And there’s plenty of performance underneath the sci-fi bodywork: Real Motors lists a 75 kW (100 hp) motor, a 15 kWh battery, a 120 mph (192 km/h) top speed, and an estimated weight of 485 lb (220 kg).

The analog analogy is spot on, with the display probably the simplest and most straightforward I’ve ever seen on an electric motorcycle. There’s also no app, no subscription, and no digital handcuffs. The bike is very much the electric equivalent of a simple ICE bike that just rides, albeit with a much nicer ride.

Unlike many of the futuristic concepts scattered around EICMA, ARES is actually headed toward limited production.

Industry observers note that real Motors looks to build just 250 examples in its first LOT 01 production run, with pricing starting at $20,000 and North American deliveries targeted for early 2027. European deliveries are expected after homologation is completed.

The tech giant has also brought former LiveWire CTO Vance Strader onto the project as it makes the difficult transition from a very cool prototype into an actual production motorcycle.

It has been revealed that I actually had the chance to do a spin on the bike, and so I’ll be reporting back on the experience. But you can tell from my smile below that the ride was quite an experience!

Seatylock has been my go-to e-bike lock company for several years now, and I use their locks for my several e-bikes and my wife’s e-bike too.

Now Seatylock has returned with some even more impressive locks. The company revealed off its fresh Ultra D28 lock, which is both angle grinder-proof and wide enough to lock the wheel of a motorcycle. It solves the problem of how do you make a lock strong enough for a motorcycle but also small and light enough that you can actually carry it with you, unlike a massive chain lock that usually stays where you park your motorcycle overnight.

In the image below, you can see the shackle next to an exposed section demonstrating the diamond coating that essentially destroys angle grinder discs – even diamond coated discs.

The company also has a slightly smaller version of the same lock designed for bicycles.

Recent findings suggest that both will absolutely destroy even the toughest angle grinder discs. Sure, eventually someone could cut through them, but it may take a dozen discs and by that point the thief has moved on to an easier target.

At EICMA 2026, Royal Enfield continued expanding its electric motorcycle ambitions with its Flying Flea sub-brand, showcasing the scrambler-style motorcycle alongside its growing lineup of lightweight, retro-inspired electric motorcycles.

There were several interesting colorways and customized designs on display, showcasing the Flying Flea’s stylish design.

The upcoming models blend Royal Enfield’s classic design heritage with modern electric technology, targeting urban riders and those looking for a fun, approachable electric motorcycle rather than a high-performance machine.

With distinctive styling, compact proportions, and an emphasis on accessible riding, the Flying Flea lineup represents Royal Enfield’s effort to carve out a place in the emerging market for smaller electric motorcycles while maintaining the character that has made its gasoline-powered bikes so popular.

Yamaha highlighted off its latest NMAX E electric scooter, bringing battery-powered performance to one of the brand’s most recognizable urban scooter families.

Designed as an electric alternative to the popular gasoline-powered NMAX, the new model combines familiar sporty styling with a quiet, low-maintenance electric drivetrain aimed at everyday city commuting.

The NMAX E uses Yamaha’s latest compact eAxle powertrain, shared with the larger-wheeled XENTER E, and delivers up to 7.5 kW (10 hp) of peak power, putting it in the 125cc-equivalent class.

With its practical step-through design, automatic operation, and approachable performance, the NMAX E represents another step in Yamaha’s push to electrify its urban mobility lineup, particularly in European markets where scooters are already a popular alternative to cars.

Segway revealed off a new vision for safer electric scooters, including its futuristic X Cruiser concept that takes rider protection to a whole new level.

Rather than relying solely on traditional motorcycle safety equipment, the X Cruiser explores automotive-inspired features such as integrated seats with seatbelts, partial enclosures, and even a fully roofed version designed to offer additional protection from the elements.

Recent findings suggest that the concept includes several configurations, ranging from a more conventional open scooter to a partially enclosed design and a fully covered model that looks like a cross between a motorcycle and a tiny electric car. While these designs are still concepts rather than production-ready scooters, they demonstrate how Segway is rethinking two-wheeled transportation by exploring ways to make electric scooters safer, more comfortable, and potentially more appealing to riders who might otherwise be hesitant to trade four wheels for two.

Eli Electric Vehicles took to EICMA 2026 to display its compact Eli Zero electric quadricycle, a tiny two-seat urban EV designed to offer much of the convenience of a car without the size, weight, or expense of a conventional automobile.

With its enclosed cabin, side-by-side seating, and ultra-compact footprint, the Eli Zero offers a practical alternative to larger vehicles for short city trips, combining the weather protection and comfort of a car with the maneuverability and efficiency of a much smaller vehicle.

Recent findings suggest that the tech giant revealed a more powerful L7e-class version of the Eli Zero that it had previously teased, expanding the vehicle’s capabilities beyond its existing L6e configuration. The new Race Edition also pushes the envelope farther with custom interior and a few extra accents to the body.

With growing interest in smaller, more efficient urban transportation, Eli’s presence at EICMA definitely underlined how the show is increasingly embracing electric mobility solutions that go beyond traditional motorcycles and scooters.

Sources indicate that NIU showed off its latest lineup of electric scooters, continuing the brand’s push to make battery-powered two-wheelers a practical alternative to gasoline-powered urban transportation. Known for its sleek designs, connected technology, and approachable electric scooters, NIU highlighted models aimed at a range of riders, from everyday city commuters to those looking for more powerful machines capable of keeping up with faster urban traffic.

The firm showed off several new models for the 2027 model year, with scooters that combine modern styling with features such as smartphone connectivity, smart security systems, and efficient electric drivetrains, all while maintaining the simplicity and low operating costs that make electric scooters so appealing.

While I didn’t see anything groundbreaking at the brand’s booth this year, the incremental updates look to push new tech features further throughout the brand’s many models, helping more of NIU’s offerings enter that premium level that the company has been known for.

For something a bit wilder, Honda shared its futuristic EV Outlier Concept, an electric motorcycle that explores what two-wheeled design could look like when engineers are freed from the constraints of traditional gasoline-powered motorcycles.

With its long, low-slung profile, radically different riding position, and futuristic bodywork, the EV Outlier looks more like something out of a science fiction movie than a conventional motorcycle. The concept features electric motors integrated into both wheels, giving it two-wheel drive while opening up fresh possibilities for packaging and weight distribution.

Rather than simply replacing a combustion engine with a battery and motor, Honda used the EV Outlier to rethink the entire motorcycle layout, demonstrating how electrification could lead to entirely fresh types of riding experiences.

While the bike remains a design concept with no confirmed production prepares, it offers an intriguing glimpse into Honda’s vision for the future of electric motorcycles.

Vespa demonstrated off its next-generation electric scooter lineup at EICMA, including electric versions of the Primavera, Sprint S, and Primavera Tech. While they don’t look radically different, there’s a lot more happening underneath the familiar steel bodywork.

A new Italian-made, rare-earth-free electric motor improves efficiency and performance, while the 45 km/h Primavera and Sprint S now feature removable batteries.

The faster 67 km/h Primavera Tech gets up to 90 km of WMTC range – a 12.5% improvement – along with an updated vehicle management system and more efficient charger.

Usually, ‘smart money’ looks to flush out poorer quality holders. It can then take on board this supply and set itself up for a possible recovery.

In this context, Bitcoin’s volatility after the NVDA rally may have offered the first real warning.

This seems to indicate that major investors are still not quite ready to enter the market. Combined with Glassnode’s data, the price action looks less like random volatility and more like strategic positioning, potentially aimed at clearing the $53k supply cluster before a stronger recovery.

Bitcoin failed to hold its post-NVDA rally, showing that buyers remain cautious.

Whale activity and the $55k supply cluster point to more downside risk before a recovery.

Sources indicate that the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) approved a rule on Nov. 23 requiring exchanges that list certain prediction market contracts to collect traders' names and employers.

When trading surges ahead of an announcement, those records could help investigators identify who traded and look for links to people or organizations with early access to the news.

The final rule also requires exchanges to disclose when covered trades occurred, at what price and size, and how the contracts settled. The CFTC indicates the reports will help it monitor trading across markets.

Under Section 16.03, exchanges must publish each covered trade’s execution time, ticker, size, and US dollar price as soon as technologically practicable.

The data must stay free for at least a year after it first appears, with instructions on how to download, save, and search it. Public trade disclosure is familiar to exchanges such as Kalshi.

Recent findings suggest that A May 13 CFTC staff letter already made prompt publication of those four fields and reporting to the CFTC under Section 16.02 conditions of relief from certain swap-reporting rules. Its updated list includes KalshiEX and Kalshi Klear.

Kalshi’s product filing identifies the exchange as a registered designated contract market. Its clearing affiliate, Kalshi Klear, told the CFTC that it clears KalshiEX’s binary event-contract swaps on a fully cash-collateralized basis.

The reporting rule covers certain event contracts classified as swaps and listed on a designated contract market.

In a recent development, A derivatives clearing organization must clear the contract and hold enough collateral at all times to cover the maximum possible loss. A covered contract can pay a fixed amount to one side, or pay both sides based on the settlement price in a structure where only one side profits.

The contract named The Weather Organization as the source for its outcome. Kalshi’s settlement record demonstrates a high of 69°F and a final No, with settlement recorded at 12:07 p.m. UTC on Nov. 24. The rule requires exchanges to publish whether the event occurred and, if it did, what happened, when it happened, and the source used to determine the outcome.

Exchanges will have to collect each trader’s name, physical address, email, phone number, occupation, and employer and associate that information with every covered order or trade.

The rule also calls for the names of account guarantors and people with a financial interest of 10% or more in the trader or account, where applicable. Exchanges must keep the data for the life of the contract and for at least five years after it ends.

The CFTC’s reporting guidebook highlights how the agency can use a customer account number to match an exchange’s trade report with a separate file that lists the trader’s occupation and employer.

It has been revealed that A link to a organization involved in an announcement could help investigators decide where to look. They would still need to establish when the information became available, whether the trader had access to it, and whether their conduct violated the relevant rule.

Hyundai is skipping the typical mid-cycle refresh and plans to launch a completely redesigned Kona, with a sleek new style and an updated high-tech interior.

It’s been nearly four years since Hyundai introduced the second-generation Kona, meaning, like most of its models, the compact SUV was expected to receive a mid-cycle refresh.

According to recent reports, hyundai is apparently going straight to the third-generation model instead. Earlier this year, early-stage prototypes were spotted in Korea that looked much boxier and more rugged than the current Kona.

Since then, several test mules have been captured testing in the US, Europe, and other regions, confirming the Kona will adopt a more upright, traditional SUV design similar to the new Santa Fe, Palisade, and Tucson.

The wider, more powerful design appears to draw inspiration from Hyundai’s off-road Crater Concept, revealed at the LA Auto Show last year.

Hyundai noted the off-road SUV Concept was a preview of the “next evolution” of its Extreme Rugged Terrain (XRT) vehicles, such as the IONIQ 5 XRT and Palisade XRT Pro. Is the Kona next in line to receive the XRT treatment?

A post shared by SHORTS CAR (@shorts_car).

Apparent leaked images from a few months ago revealed a design that looked like a mashup of the Crater Concept and IONIQ 5, with pixelated lighting and a clamshell hood.

Most recently, the third-gen Hyundai Kona, codenamed “SX3,” was spotted disguised in a parking garage in Korea. The images were sent to ShortsCar, revealing the latest Kona’s wheel design.

In a recent development, while earlier reports suggested Hyundai planned to drop the all-electric Kona variant and would only offer gas and hybrid versions, the prototype captured in Korea is expected to be the EV model. However, Hyundai has yet to confirm powertrain or battery specs.

It has been revealed that the updates are even more evident on the inside. Previous spy images appeared to show the third-gen Hyundai Kona running Hyundai’s upcoming Pleos Connect infotainment system, like the IONIQ 3.

In the IONIQ 3, Hyundai offers a 12.9″ or 14.6″ center infotainment screen, plus an optional driver display.

Like the current model, the third-gen Kona is expected to be available with fully electric (EV), hybrid, and gas-powered powertrains.

While Hyundai skipped the 2026 Kona EV, the electric version could return in 2027 or 2028 when the third-generation model is expected to arrive.

The hybrid version will likely use the same 1.6L hybrid engine as the fresh Seltos, while the EV variant could offer similar powertrain and battery options to the IONIQ 3.

The IONIQ 3 is available with two battery packs in Europe and the UK: 42 kWh and 61 kWh, offering WLTP ranges of up to 213 miles (344 km) and 308 miles (497 km), respectively.

  • Recent findings suggest that the firm expanded from five available cryptocurrencies to eight on Nov.
  • customers can trade these three tokens on the Fidelity website and app.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fidelity Investments now supports three newly introduced cryptocurrencies on its retail crypto trading platform: Chainlink (LINK), Aave (AAVE) and Uniswap (UNI).

Recent findings suggest that the firm expanded from five available cryptocurrencies to eight on Nov. 24. In just one day, Fidelity added the same number of digital assets that it had added in the four years since it first made Bitcoin and Ether available for customer trading.

Eligible U.S. customers can trade these three tokens on the Fidelity website and app. Some states may have limited access to Fidelity's services.

Recent findings suggest that fidelity's three new listings include tokens that represent different areas of decentralized finance. Aave is a lending protocol where users can deposit crypto assets to earn interest or use them as collateral for loans. AAVE token holders can vote on changes to the protocol's lending markets and other aspects of its operation.

Sources indicate that uniswap is a decentralized trading platform where users can trade different tokens using shared pools of assets provided by other users. UNI is the Uniswap governance token.

It has been revealed that chainlink provides the data that blockchain apps need to operate. For example, a lending protocol might use a Chainlink price feed to assess the value of collateral for a borrower's loan. Chainlink (LINK) tokens are used to pay for services provided on its network.

Fidelity Crypto started accepting customers from its waitlist in November 2022. At the time, the only two cryptocurrencies it offered were Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH). By March 2023, Fidelity was offering its service to more eligible U.S. investors, but these were still the only cryptocurrencies it allowed customers to trade.

On July 17, 2024, Fidelity added Litecoin (LTC) to its list of cryptocurrencies, bringing the total to three. Over a year later, on Oct. 23, 2025, the organization introduced Solana (SOL). In addition to individual retail accounts, Solana became available for crypto IRAs, wealth managers and institutional clients.

Fidelity added its fifth cryptocurrency on Feb. 4, 2026, when it released Fidelity Digital Dollar (FIDD) as its first stablecoin available to retail and institutional investors. Eligible customers can exchange or redeem each FIDD token for $1. Fidelity waives its usual crypto trading fee when users exchange FIDD for dollars.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla is now only selling one version of the Cybertruck in the US: the tri-motor Cyberbeast, which just got another $7,500 price hike to $109,990.
  • Industry observers note that the Dual Motor and Premium AWD trims are still listed on Tesla’s configurator, but both are greyed out and can’t be selected.
  • Here’s what Tesla’s US configurator shows today with a Los Angeles delivery address:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla is now only selling one version of the Cybertruck in the US: the tri-motor Cyberbeast, which just got another $7,500 price hike to $109,990.

Industry observers note that the Dual Motor and Premium AWD trims are still listed on Tesla’s configurator, but both are greyed out and can’t be selected. So the cheapest Cybertruck you can order today costs $109,990, up 57% from $69,990 in early August.

Here’s what Tesla’s US configurator shows today with a Los Angeles delivery address:.

A week ago, the Cyberbeast cost $102,490. Before that, it was $99,990. That’s a $10,000 (10%) increase in about a week on a truck that hasn’t changed: 320 miles of estimated range, 11,000 lbs of towing, and 0-60 mph in 2.6 seconds.

It has been revealed that on November 6, the same day Elon Musk announced the end of Cybertruck production, Tesla raised Cybertruck prices by up to 10% and paused orders for the base Dual Motor. That made the $92,490 Premium AWD the entry point. Now it’s gone too, with no announcement. The configurator just stopped letting you pick it.

Recent findings suggest that fresh inventory isn’t an alternative either. When we checked, Tesla’s inventory search demonstrated no new Cybertrucks within 200 miles of Los Angeles.

This comes two days after Musk extended Cybertruck production through the end of summer 2027 to “work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog.” On Monday, he claimed the order rate “far exceeds” production and that Tesla would “have to return deposits for a lot of people.”.

It has been revealed that if there really is a backlog, cutting off the two cheaper trims is one way to cap it before the line shuts down. It also pushes whatever demand is left toward the most expensive, highest-margin version of the truck.

According to recent reports, but the sales data doesn’t describe a truck with a demand problem in the other direction. We estimate Tesla delivered 7,000 to 8,000 Cybertrucks in Q3, a pace of about 30,000 a year on a line with more than 125,000 units of installed capacity. And in February, Tesla was offering a dual-motor Cybertruck at $59,990 for “only the next 10 days.”.

According to recent reports, that’s $50,000 less than the cheapest Cybertruck you can order today. Nine months later.

Some of those $59,990 buyers are still waiting on delivery dates pushed into 2027. Tesla hasn’t mentioned whether their orders, or any other Dual Motor and Premium orders in the queue, will be built before production ends.

Unlike the thousands of $59k CT orders that may never get manufactured I can guarantee that every high margin $110k CyberBeast order will be delivered before production ends.

It has been revealed that this is the wind-down playbook, and it’s moving faster than I expected. Announce the end, raise prices, pull the cheaper trims, and sell the last trucks in their most expensive form. Tesla is squeezing as much as it can out of every remaining Cybertruck.

I don’t blame Tesla for wanting margin on a program it’s walking away from. But it makes the “order backlog” talk look like what we said it was: an end-of-life rush Tesla created by announcing the end, now being monetized with a $109,990 sticker. Not great for anyone who was told in 2019 that this truck would start at $39,900, or that the tri-motor version would cost $69,900.

If you want a Cybertruck that isn’t a Cyberbeast, you’re now shopping used. And I’d keep an eye on used prices, because a truck that’s going out of production with no cheaper fresh option could hold its value better than it has over the last two years.

#110902. End of Crypto Trading? How AI Replaces Ones Who Pumped Bitcoin (BTC)

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (741 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 U ↗ Open Full Page

End of Crypto Trading? How AI Replaces Ones Who Pumped Bitcoin (BTC)

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (741 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: U

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the “pump” trade could be taken to new extremes.
  • All things considered, agents may exacerbate many of the existing complications with crypto, from short lived moves/reversals, to dangerous herding and even more pronounced drawdowns.
  • Automation is not necessarily a new occurrence in the space, from simple rule-based trading (implement a certain set of rules when X occurs) to algo trading (use algos to spread out trading activity to avoid market impact), but it appears to be shifting from humans implementing strategies to letting AI make decisions and execute.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the “pump” trade could be taken to new extremes. While some may still be able to use their influence to promote a token, causing others to pile in, it could now be left up to AI to scour socials/wallet activity for abnormal trading volume, assess momentum rankings, etc. and execute on these opportunities faster than those that may be slower to react.

All things considered, agents may exacerbate many of the existing complications with crypto, from short lived moves/reversals, to dangerous herding and even more pronounced drawdowns.

Automation is not necessarily a new occurrence in the space, from simple rule-based trading (implement a certain set of rules when X occurs) to algo trading (use algos to spread out trading activity to avoid market impact), but it appears to be shifting from humans implementing strategies to letting AI make decisions and execute.

A February 2026 study from the Journal of Futures Markets found sub-second trading patterns in BTC/ETH perpetual/spot markets exhibiting behavior consistent with algo trading for liquidity, increasing volatility and trading costs with no significant impact on prices.

In August 2026, Binance rolled out Agent OS allowing builders to access exchange trading functionality and data via AI agents.

Coinbase Ventures released a comprehensive breakdown of the crypto agentic stack from data, to agent building tools, to execution/compliance in November. Instead of dictating each trade, owners may be able to assign high-level goals (i.e. follow momentum, hedge position, etc.) for agents to implement 24/7.

In a recent development, automation will likely accelerate across the crypto space. While macro events, ETF inflows/outflows, large holders, etc. will still have an impact on Bitcoin, it’s likely that many more aspects/trades will become automated.

Time will tell how pervasive agentic trading will become, but the era of a small group of traders/influencers/chat rooms able to move the needle via FOMO/hype seems poised to face stiff competition from AI that never sleeps.

AI is not necessarily intelligent. A 2026 study published in the journal Frontiers in Blockchain studied machine-learning strategies using crypto market data and found that many strategies became highly overfit and offered no viable edge for retail traders once realistic trading fees were taken into account.

Also, strategies that performed well on one cryptocurrency did not necessarily perform well on others. Faster processing speeds can’t make bad data good, can’t identify all false narratives and can’t insulate a strategy from sudden shifts in market regimes.

Are institutional investors still relevant? Can they protect themselves? Absolutely.

Institutions are (and will continue to be) an important source of capital, liquidity and price discovery (particularly for Bitcoin). A 2026 study using BTC data from 2012–2025 found that as the market has matured, Bitcoin has seen increased trading volume, decreasing transaction costs and increasing market efficiency.

Sources indicate that wintermute reported that in the first half of 2026 institutional clients accounted for 72% of total spot trading volume on its OTC desk (note: this is Wintermute’s OTC desk and is not representative of the entire market). It’s also worth noting that many institutional investors do employ quantitative strategies and state-of-the-art execution technologies.

While larger investors may have access to better data, faster infrastructure, cross-venue surveillance capabilities and stricter risk management protocols (and can limit their exposure and monitor abnormal order flow), there’s only so much that institutional investors can do to protect themselves.

Sources indicate that institutional investors can’t control a 24/7 global market with liquidity spread across multiple venues and derivatives markets. They also can’t assume that all AIs are created equal/safe (as Binance’s launch of its own AI demonstrated prompt injection risks and limited visibility into external AIs’ trading logic/reasons for trading).

Finally, during times of stress, risk management/contingency protocols (used by many investors) could be a crowded exit for funds that employ similar strategies.

According to recent reports, the future is not “AI replaces every trader.” It will likely see continued automation of certain aspects of trading (i.e. execution, short-term alpha hunting, etc.) and a continued shift in the value-add that humans bring to the table (i.e. capital allocation, risk management, original research, granting/trading bots permission to trade, etc.).

While AI/bots may continue to squeeze spreads in normal market conditions, they may exacerbate drawdowns/cascades during times of market stress as strategies compete with one another.

At the end of the day, Bitcoin will still be bought/sold, it’s just a question of who gets to make those decisions.

  • Luxor’s weekly mining revision put the seven-day average hashrate at 1,033 EH/s, up 7.8% from 959 EH/s a week earlier.
  • According to recent reports, over the same week, dollar hashprice fell 3%, from $30.27 to $29.36 per petahash per second per day.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that bitcoin’s hashrate rebounded above 1,000 exahashes per second in the week to Nov. 23, while the expected dollar revenue per unit of that computing power fell over the same week.

Luxor’s weekly mining revision put the seven-day average hashrate at 1,033 EH/s, up 7.8% from 959 EH/s a week earlier.

According to recent reports, over the same week, dollar hashprice fell 3%, from $30.27 to $29.36 per petahash per second per day. Hashprice is the gross daily revenue a miner can expect from a fixed amount of computing power, before electricity and other costs.

The rebound came with Bitcoin trading near $60,000 on Nov. 24, about 52.5% below its October 2025 price record. The 30-day average hashrate was about 1,013 EH/s on Nov. 23, or 91.2% of the roughly 1,110 EH/s high recorded on Nov. 11, 2025, in the period analyzed.

The average had fallen to 896 EH/s on July 28, about 19.3% below that high.

The same point in the two previous Bitcoin bear markets gives that 91% some context.

The comparison uses the 30-day average 413 days after each cycle’s peak daily price close, measured against the highest 30-day hashrate recorded between the price peak and day 413.

It also uses Blockchain.com’s daily estimates, with Coin Metrics readings filling three missing dates in November 2025. A 30-day average smooths swings when blocks arrive more rapidly or slowly by chance.

In the 2017–18 cycle, mining power kept rising after the December 2017 price peak. It reached 52.4 EH/s in October 2018, then fell to 37.6 EH/s on Dec. 25. By Feb. 2, 2019, the matched date, it had recovered to 41.9 EH/s, just under 80% of its high.

In the 2021–22 cycle, hashrate also set a high well after the price peak, reaching 265.2 EH/s in November 2022. It stood at 246.8 EH/s on Dec. 26, 2022, or 93.1% of its high. Today’s network is slightly farther below its peak than it was at that point in 2022 and closer than it was after the 2018 slump.

Recent findings suggest that bitcoin’s 30-day network hashrate as a share of its cycle high, measured 413 days after each peak daily price close. Each high is the strongest 30-day estimate from the price peak through the comparison date.

Source: Blockchain.com 2017–19 · · Blockchain.com 2020–22 · · Blockchain.com 2024–26 · · Coin Metrics, November 2025 · · Galaxy Research, price peaks · · Blockchain.com, methodology.

According to recent reports, hashrate Index recorded a 2022 hashprice low of $55.94 per petahash per second per day, almost twice its Nov. 23 reading. The April 2024 halving cut Bitcoin’s fixed subsidy from 6.25 to 3.125 BTC per block. Transaction fees add to that subsidy, but they made up just 0.64% of block rewards in Luxor’s latest weekly snapshot.

In a recent development, bitcoin’s mining difficulty fell 9.13% on Nov. 14. Using power prices and machine economics, Luxor’s West Texas analysis estimated that miners cutting electricity use there could account for roughly three-quarters of the 91 EH/s drop in the network’s 14-day average around that adjustment.

Riot Platforms previously earned credits for reducing power use.

Core Scientific’s third-quarter results show $215.4 million in quarterly colocation revenue, and the manufacturer was billing for 485 megawatts of capacity as of Sept. 30.

IREN stated its Horizon 1 facility entered service for Microsoft during the September quarter. The company’s mining revenue fell to $28 million from $67 million in the previous quarter.

Riot’s November results show the organization mined 1,637 BTC in the third quarter, up from 1,406 a year earlier, and separately disclosed a 910-megawatt powered-land lease for AI at Corsicana with the first delivery scheduled for September 2027.

A sustained loss of mining power would lengthen the expected time between blocks at the prevailing difficulty.

Bitcoin adjusts the difficulty every 2,016 blocks to bring the pace back toward one block every 10 minutes.

At a lower hashrate, the network would still add less proof of work over a given span of time. The latest weekly rebound shows that computing power can rise even as mining revenue per unit falls.

Sources indicate that A sustained drop in computing power changes how quickly blocks arrive. Bitcoin can adjust difficulty when the current period ends.

The expected block interval can recover after a retarget while computing power remains lower.

Tech Report: Volkswagen is delaying another EV based on the SSP

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (632 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After delaying development of the long-awaited electric Golf, Volkswagen is delaying another EV based on its SSP platform.
  • As it scrambles to cut costs, Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer revealed in an internal memo at the end of October that development of the all-electric Golf is being delayed at its Wolfsburg plant in Germany.
  • The news comes after the VW Group posted an operating loss of €5.9 billion ($6.5 billion) in the third quarter, its largest quarterly loss since the infamous Dieselgate scandal in 2015.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After delaying development of the long-awaited electric Golf, Volkswagen is delaying another EV based on its SSP platform.

As it scrambles to cut costs, Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer revealed in an internal memo at the end of October that development of the all-electric Golf is being delayed at its Wolfsburg plant in Germany.

The news comes after the VW Group posted an operating loss of €5.9 billion ($6.5 billion) in the third quarter, its largest quarterly loss since the infamous Dieselgate scandal in 2015.

“We simply can’t afford this work right now,” Schäfer mentioned in the memo reviewed by Reuters. The Wolfsburg plant, AKA the “heart of the VW brand,” is about €300 million ($334.5 million) short of its cost-cutting targets, the memo said.

Volkswagen initially planned to launch the Golf EV in 2028, but Schäfer confirmed earlier this year that the long-awaited electric car was delayed until closer to 2030.

Schäfer suggested the delay was because the SSP (Scalable Systems Platform), which is being developed through its partnership with Rivian, was taking longer than expected, again due to costs.

According to Autocar, Volkswagen is now delaying the Audi A4 E-tron as well, another vehicle that was initially planned to be among the first based on the SSP platform.

Production of the electric A4 is being pushed back until at least 2029, a year later than originally planned. While the delay is disappointing for Audi fans (including myself) still waiting for an electric A4, it also puts Audi behind rival luxury brands in the mid-size sedan segment.

BMW has the upcoming i3, and Mercedes-Benz has the C-Class EV, both of which feature major improvements in range, charging, and efficiency over their previous-generation EVs.

Volkswagen said in 2023 that the 800V SSP will serve as a “single future backbone with integrated electric and electronics architecture,” claiming that more than 40 million models were expected to be built on it.

The company also mentioned investment and R&D costs were expected to be reduced by about 30% compared to the current MEB platform, enabling most models “to achieve the same margin compared to their conventionally powered counterparts.”.

Volkswagen’s software struggles started in its internal division, Cariad, leading to delays, missed targets, and budget overruns.

To fix it, VW turned to Rivian, forming a joint venture to develop its next-gen software-defined vehicle (SDV) electrical architecture.

In March, VW noted several test vehicles, including the ID.EVERY1, Audi, and Scout with the SDV architecture underwent “comprehensive evaluation,” and successfully validated over-the-air (OTA) functionality.

Being cash efficient is good, but delays to the next-gen platform that will keep you competitive with rival brands seem like a problem.

According to recent reports, however, the Audi A4 E-tron delay is not entirely about software. The Autocar report claims Audi demanded significant changes to the SSP platform for the A4 E-tron so it more closely matched the current gas version.

Audi reportedly wanted individual footwells for front and rear passengers, which would require repositioning the battery.

The luxury brand also reportedly asked for a 48V electrical system instead of the traditional 12V setup initially planned.

While development of the Golf EV is on hold, VW’s works council noted the pause will not delay its launch, promising to make up for lost time. It’s still expected to launch in 2030. The Audi A4 E-tron is now expected to arrive around 2029.
