📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Wall Street Journal reported on Nov. 24 that the US was preparing higher tariffs on China, the European Union, and other trading partners, which could impact Bitcoin.

Citing people familiar with the intends, the Journal reported that US Trade Representative (USTR) Jamieson Greer could release the findings of a months-long investigation into manufacturing overcapacity as soon as this week.

It has been revealed that on Nov. 24, the USTR docket still demonstrated the investigation opened in March and four days of hearings in May, listing no determination or tariff schedule for the case. A check of published USTR notices in the Federal Register found none dated Nov. 19 through Nov. 24.

Recent findings suggest that the available White House, Treasury, and Commerce trade agency listings carried no announcement of the action described in the report. Importers still have no published list of the goods that would face these duties, the rates that would apply or the date they would start.

According to recent reports, on Nov. 20, Greer told Bloomberg Television he expected the work to be finished by year-end. He declined to specify which economies might face additional tariffs.

USTR opened the investigations on March 11 under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 and is examining whether policies such as subsidies sustain more manufacturing capacity than demand supports and whether those practices burden or restrict US commerce.

Recent findings suggest that the agency’s fact sheet described the sectors it wanted to examine. An investigation of how a product is made or subsidized leaves open which products, if any, may face duties.

Industry observers note that the inquiry covers 16 economies, including the EU. The March 17 initiation notice also lists Singapore, Switzerland, Norway, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, South Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Mexico, Japan and India. Hearings ran from May 5 through May 8.

Industry observers note that under Section 304 of the Trade Act, USTR must determine whether the practices are actionable. If it makes an affirmative finding, it must decide what action, if any, to take. The law requires the trade representative to publish the determination and the facts it rests on in the Federal Register.

It has been revealed that public hearings ended in May. The USTR docket still indicated no determination on Nov. 24.

A USTR determination would establish whether the practices are actionable and, if so, what action USTR should take.

In a recent development, scope is the public docket checked on Nov. 24, 2026. Marker spacing shows the order of events and does not measure elapsed time. No tariff outcome is assumed.

The dates come from USTR’s initiation release and case docket. The lower diagram reveals the determination and publication requirements in Section 304 of the Trade Act.

Scope is the public docket checked on Nov. 24, 2026. Marker spacing highlights the order of events and does not measure elapsed time. No tariff outcome is assumed.

On July 23, USTR announced final duties on 60 economies after separate investigations into their failures to impose and enforce bans on imports made with forced labor.

On April 9, 2025, President Donald Trump posted that he had authorized a 90-day pause in some higher tariffs while raising the rate for China.

The executive order dated the same day amended the tariff schedule and applied the changes to covered goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, at or after 12:01 a.m. Eastern daylight time on April 10.

The reciprocal tariff changes came under different authority from the current investigation.

The written terms tell the company whether its goods fall under the amended tariff schedule and whether its shipment enters before or after the cutoff. The applicable rate can depend on those details and on whether an exemption applies.

Industry observers note that after Trump signaled a possible tariff increase on China in October 2025, Bitcoin fell during a broader selloff. That episode reveals why a tariff headline can impact crypto investors before importers have any new duties to enter on customs paperwork.

Sources indicate that if the USTR determination leads to tariffs, the product coverage, rates, and entry dates will show where costs change and when. Until USTR publishes its findings, the docket remains the place to look for the public decision.

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Bitcoinmagazine ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: UniCredit Opens Bitcoin to Italian Savers, Capping Gains at 65%

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (578 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bitcoinmagazine

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • UniCredit began selling a six-year, capital-protected certificate linked to BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin ETP to retail clients in Italy, with gains capped at 65%.
  • UniCredit on Tuesday began selling a capital-protected certificate that lets retail clients in Italy follow the bitcoin price, a product the bank calls the first investment solution of its kind in the country.
  • According to recent reports, the six-year, euro-denominated certificate will be listed on the Munich stock exchange and is linked to the iShares Bitcoin ETP managed by BlackRock, UniCredit noted in a release.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UniCredit began selling a six-year, capital-protected certificate linked to BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin ETP to retail clients in Italy, with gains capped at 65%.

UniCredit on Tuesday began selling a capital-protected certificate that lets retail clients in Italy follow the bitcoin price, a product the bank calls the first investment solution of its kind in the country.

According to recent reports, the six-year, euro-denominated certificate will be listed on the Munich stock exchange and is linked to the iShares Bitcoin ETP managed by BlackRock, UniCredit noted in a release. The placement period runs from Nov. 24 to Dec. 18, 2026.

The note is open only to UniCredit Italia retail clients with specific characteristics, and only through the bank’s advisory service. It can’t be bought independently or by investors who aren’t UniCredit clients, and the minimum investment is €1,000, Italian newswire Teleborsa reported.

A capital-protected certificate is a structured note. The issuing bank promises to repay the original investment at maturity and pays a return tied to an underlying asset, in this case bitcoin through the BlackRock product. Buyers hold a claim on the bank, not bitcoin itself.

Sources indicate that if bitcoin is down at maturity, holders get 100% of their capital back. If it rises, they share in the gain up to a maximum return of 65% on the capital invested. Before maturity, the certificate’s price follows market conditions, so the protection applies only at the end of the six years.

That cap works out to roughly 8.7% a year at most, no matter how far bitcoin climbs. And because the certificate is UniCredit’s own debt, the protection depends on the bank’s ability to pay. Documents for a similar UniCredit note in Germany state that no third-party guarantee covers an issuer default.

“With the launch of this certificate, UniCredit is writing a new page of financial innovation in the country, confirming its market leadership,” said Chicco Di Stasi, Head of Group Investment Product Solutions at UniCredit.

“Diversification is no longer just a prudential rule, but the key to capturing the value of the future,” Di Stasi said, adding that the bank is responding to growing client demand and offering the product to Italian savers “for the very first time.”.

Di Stasi stated the bank is bringing to Italy “a pioneering model already proven by its success in Germany and Austria.” Those earlier notes are denominated in dollars and track BlackRock’s U.S.-listed iShares Bitcoin Trust instead.

HypoVereinsbank, UniCredit’s German unit, sold a version to private clients in March with a 160% cap, or 60% upside. UniCredit Bank Austria debuted its own six-year note in April with a 175% cap, or 75% upside. Italy’s 65% falls between the two.

Sources indicate that the bank has moved into bitcoin in steps. It first offered a capital-protected bitcoin product to professional clients only in 2025. In May, it placed a bitcoin and ether certificate for professional clients with a €100,000 minimum.

It has been revealed that in September, UniCredit was reported to be weighing crypto custody, including the infrastructure to hold and trade digital assets. Elsewhere in Italy, Banca Sella became the first Italian bank licensed for crypto services under MiCA in May.

It has been revealed that uniCredit is one of Europe’s largest banks. It reported €918.3 billion in total assets at Sept. 30 and a record €3.3 billion in third-quarter net profit.

Bitcoin traded near $60,400 on Tuesday, more than 50% below its record above $126,000.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, wallets attributed to Uphold accounted for about 82% of the 545.3 million XRP decline in tracked exchange balances in the seven days to Nov. 24.

Industry observers note that the weekly balance breakdown from XRP Insights compares the same addresses on Nov. 17 and Nov. 24. At the end of the week, the tracker counted about 1.25 billion XRP in 24 Uphold-attributed wallets.

Three payments from Uphold-labeled addresses sent about 270 million XRP to three unlabeled wallets on Nov. 23. At follow-up checks the next day, each still held roughly 90 million tokens.

The broader snapshot at 08:01 UTC on Nov. 24 put exchange-attributed holdings at 21.69 billion XRP across 708 addresses. The weekly calculation used the 707 wallets already tracked on Nov. 17.

Coinbase-attributed balances fell by 35.9 million XRP, and Bithumb’s fell by 24.7 million, while Binance-attributed wallets added about 181,000.

Nov. 17–24, 2026 comparison across the same 707 XRP Ledger wallets tracked by XRP Insights.

Uphold-attributed wallets accounted for about 82% of the net decline across the 24 tracked exchanges.

In a recent development, public labels group XRP Ledger wallets by attributed exchange. The comparison uses the same addresses at both dates and includes custody balances. It measures a net change in those balances.

The Uphold share is 446,819,576.34 divided by 545,288,925.25 XRP. The other exchanges’ combined decline is the difference, 98,469,348.91 XRP. Bar lengths use the unrounded proportion. XRP amounts are rounded to one decimal million and the share to a whole percent.

Sources indicate that public labels group XRP Ledger wallets by attributed exchange. The comparison uses the same addresses at both dates and includes custody balances. It measures a net change in those balances.

Recent findings suggest that between 16:21:22 and 16:21:42 UTC on Nov. 23, the XRP Ledger recorded three successful payments from three separate addresses labeled Uphold by XRPSCAN.

The first payment, second payment, and third payment each delivered just over 90 million XRP. Each sending address was left with 1 token, and each receiving address held about 40 tokens before the transfers.

The account histories for rhDoUm, rP2Sxx and rKB4EP show one subsequent incoming payment of 0.000010 XRP to each wallet. No outgoing transaction appeared by the time XRPSCAN balances were checked between 13:12 and 13:13 UTC on Nov. 24.

In a recent development, on Nov. 20, one unlabeled address sent 50 XRP to each of the three. Later that day, each sent 10 tokens to the same Uphold-labeled address.

Those payments establish a connection among the addresses, but Uphold’s public transparency report names none of the three recipients.

In a recent development, XRPSONAR’s Nov. 23 flow series counted 271.6 million XRP sent from its known Uphold wallets and 2.4 million received, leaving a net outflow of 269.2 million tokens that day.

The same series showed a separate 178.7 million XRP net outflow on Nov. 20.

In October, XRP Insights attributed most of an earlier monthly decline to Uphold moving tokens into newly used wallets outside the tracked set. The labeled balance can fall even when the exchange still controls the coins.

A useful test would compare how much was offered within the same distance of the market midpoint on the same spot pairs and venues at comparable times before and after Nov. 23.

Measuring buy orders over the same price range would show how much a seller could trade near the quoted price.

Repeated readings would show whether any difference in quoted depth persisted beyond a single snapshot. A thinner set of sell orders in that range would show that buyers could get less XRP close to the prevailing quote on those markets.

Tech Report: BYD’s new flagship Tang SUV starts at about $34,000 with two enormous screens

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (624 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • BYD opened pre-orders for the third-generation Tang starting at about $34,000 in China.
  • The third-generation Tang joins the Great Tang, or Da Tang, as it’s called in China in BYD’s expanding flagship SUV lineup.
  • We knew it was coming soon after the newly introduced model appeared in a regulatory filing in China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) last month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD opened pre-orders for the third-generation Tang starting at about $34,000 in China. This five-seat flagship SUV packs more than you’d expect for the money, with two massive 30-inch-plus screens inside and up to 850 km (528 miles) of CLTC range.

The third-generation Tang joins the Great Tang, or Da Tang, as it’s called in China in BYD’s expanding flagship SUV lineup.

We knew it was coming soon after the newly introduced model appeared in a regulatory filing in China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) last month.

BYD unveiled on Friday that pre-orders for the third-gen Tang are officially open, starting at 225,000 yuan, which is around $34,000.

The “large five-seat flagship SUV,” as BYD calls it, is available in three variants, priced from 225,000 yuan ($34,000), 240,000 yuan ($36,000), and 260,000 yuan ($39,000) with rear- and all-wheel-drive variants.

The two lower-priced variants are both RWD, offering a CLTC range of up to 850 km (528 miles), while the top-spec dual-motor AWD version has up to 770 km (478 miles).

All versions use BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging tech, enabling the battery to be charged from 10% to 80% in five minutes, or nine minutes to go from 10% to 97%.

Recent findings suggest that inside, the five-seat SUV packs a surprising amount of tech and premium extras for the price. The setup features two massive screens: a 35.4″ integrated display and another 30″ panoramic theater screen.

Unlike its predessor, which offered five and six-seat configurations, the third-gen Tang will only be offered as a five-seater.

The five-seat setup opens up interior space for passengers and the third-gen Tang has the largest front trunk (frunk) in its class at 205L, BYD noted.

Like many of its new flagship vehicles, the third-gen Tang is equipped with BYD’s latest tech, including its God’s Eye B driver-assistance system and Disus-A dual-chamber intelligent air suspension body control system.

Other added features include a 22-speaker Dynaudio sound system, intelligent electric all‑wheel drive, a high-speed tire blowout stability system, and its iTAC intelligent torque control system.

Lu Tian, the general manager of BYD’s Dynasty division noted third-gen Tang vehicles have arrived at dealerships nationwide.

Sources indicate that why mention "two enormous screens" like they are some markers of a more premium vehicle or represent some value? We don't measure the utility of cars by screen real estate per dollar. It's the other part of the utility that matter: range, driving dynamics, road trip convenience, fit/finish/materials/insulation. Personally, I don't think "enormous screens" are going to age well as an automotive trend.

The Great Tang received over 150,000 preorders by the time it launched in mid-June, a record for a single BYD model.

Since its official launch, the larger Great Tang (Da Tang) has sold more than 10,000 units for four straight months now.

The Great Tang is on sale in China in pure electric (EV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains. The cheapest EV variant starts at 239,900 yuan ($35,500) a CLTC driving range of 800 km (497 miles). Starting at just 269,900 yuan ($40,000), the Flagship EV version uses a bigger (130.15 kWh) battery, offering a CLTC range of up to 590 miles (950 km).

Sources indicate that will BYD’s smaller five-seat SUV draw the same demand? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.
